title: CPT 90791 vs 90792: Psychiatric Diagnostic Evaluation Billing and Documentation (2026)
summary: 90791 vs 90792 comes down to medical services: who can bill each psychiatric diagnostic evaluation code, untimed and frequency rules, same-day NCCI edits, the 90785 add-on, documentation by code, common denials and 2026 Medicare rates.
body_markdown:
CPT 90791 is a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. CPT 90792 is the same evaluation with medical services, such as physical exam elements, prescribing or ordering labs, so it's generally limited to physicians and to nurse practitioners, physician assistants and clinical nurse specialists working within state scope. Both codes are untimed and billed once per day, and Medicare won't pay either one alongside psychotherapy or an E/M visit by the same provider on the same date.


Below: who can bill each code, what "untimed" means, frequency limits at Medicare, two Medicaid programs and a commercial plan, same-day NCCI rules, 90785, documentation, 2026 payment and denials. For the time-based codes that usually follow an intake, see our guide to[psychotherapy CPT codes 90832, 90834 and 90837](https://blog.adentris.com/psychotherapy-cpt-codes-90832-90834-90837/) .


The short version


- 90792 adds a medical assessment to 90791, so the clinician's license has to cover medical work. LCSWs, counselors, MFTs and most psychologists bill 90791.
- Both codes are untimed: one unit per day, however long the evaluation runs. Separate evaluations with the patient and with informants on different days can each be reported.
- Under the 2026 NCCI Policy Manual, neither code is billed with psychotherapy or an E/M service on the same date by the same provider. The 90785 add-on is allowed.
- Medicare treats the evaluation as a once-per-episode service, repeatable after a treatment break of about 6 months, an inpatient admission or a significant change. Medicaid and commercial plans often cap it at one per provider per year.
- 2026 Medicare national office amounts are $173.35 for 90791 and $202.08 for 90792. Facility rates for both fell from 2025.


## What 90791 and 90792 describe


Both codes cover the same core work. First Coast's psychiatric codes LCD (L33252) calls the basic evaluation "an integrated biopsychosocial assessment": history, psychiatric history, a complete mental status exam, a tentative diagnosis and a judgment about whether the patient can and will take part in treatment.


90792 adds the medical layer: physical exam elements as indicated, and possibly prescribing and reviewing or ordering labs and other studies. CMS's NCCI manual puts it bluntly. 90791 is the evaluation without medical E&M, and 90792 is the evaluation with medical E&M.


Code Descriptor What it includes Typical billers 2026 Medicare national (office / facility)


**90791** Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation History, mental status exam, diagnosis, treatment recommendations Psychiatrists, psychologists, LCSWs, counselors, MFTs, psychiatric NPs $173.35 / $137.28


**90792** Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services Everything in 90791, plus exam elements, prescribing, labs and other studies Physicians, and NPs, PAs and CNSs within state scope $202.08 / $159.32


**+90785** Interactive complexity (add-on) Communication factors that complicate the service Whoever bills the primary code $14.70 / $11.69


For the wider code set, see our[CPT codes guide for behavioral health](https://blog.adentris.com/cpt-codes-behavioral-health-guide/) .


### What "untimed" means


Neither descriptor carries a time. That cuts both ways. There's no minimum to reach, unlike the 16, 38 and 53-minute psychotherapy thresholds, and no extra unit for a long intake: a 50-minute evaluation and a two-hour one are each a single unit. WPS's psychiatry LCD (L34616) allows one evaluation per day, and Medicare's practitioner MUE for each code is one unit.


Long evaluations are handled by days, not minutes. L34616 allows separate evaluations with the patient and with other informants, so a parent interview on Monday and the child's interview on Wednesday can each be billed under the patient's name. We'd still record start and stop times. If a clinician bills six in one day, the times should add up.


## Who can bill 90791 and 90792


The test is scope of license, not job title. A clinician licensed to diagnose mental illness can generally bill 90791. 90792 needs a license that covers medical services: First Coast's billing article (A57520) frames it as an option for "the physician or non-physician practitioner," who may use 90792 or an E/M code.


Practitioner (Medicare) 90791 90792 Medicare pays


Physician (psychiatry, addiction medicine, primary care) Yes Yes 100% of the fee schedule


Nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist Yes Yes, within state scope 85% of the physician amount


Physician assistant Yes Yes, within state scope and supervision rules 85% of the physician amount


Clinical psychologist Yes Generally no 100% of the fee schedule


Clinical social worker Yes No 75% of the clinical psychologist amount


Marriage and family therapist, mental health counselor (since January 1, 2024) Yes No 75% of the clinical psychologist amount


"Generally no" for psychologists is deliberate: Indiana Medicaid lets an HSPP (health service provider in psychology) render 90792. When the NPI, taxonomy and license on the claim don't fit the code, expect a provider-type denial.


### 90792 or a new-patient E/M visit?


Prescribers have a real choice. WPS's billing article (A57480) allows an E/M service in place of the initial interview if the E/M's required elements are met. It matters when the prescriber also does psychotherapy at intake: 90792 can't be billed with psychotherapy that day, but an E/M can carry the add-ons 90833, 90836 or 90838 when both services are significant and separately identifiable.


At 2026 national office rates, 90792 pays $202.08. A level 4 new-patient visit (99204) pays $177.36, and adding 30 minutes of psychotherapy (90833) brings the pair to $258.86. That gap isn't a reason to switch codes. It's a reason to code what happened, choosing the E/M level on medical decision making rather than time, as A57480 requires when psychotherapy add-ons are billed.


### Medicaid programs that want H0031 or H0001


Some Medicaid programs and managed care plans route non-physician assessments to H0031 (mental health assessment, by non-physician) or H0001 (alcohol and/or drug assessment). Both are status I, not valid for Medicare, in the 2026 fee schedule file. The state manual and MCO contract decide. In SUD programs, the assessment you bill should agree with the level of care decision, as our[ASAM documentation guide](https://blog.adentris.com/asam-level-of-care-documentation-guide/) explains.


## How often you can bill an evaluation


Medicare treats the evaluation as an onset-of-illness service. First Coast (L33252) and WPS (A57480) both allow it once at onset, with a repeat by the same provider after a treatment break of approximately 6 months. First Coast also allows a repeat for an inpatient psychiatric admission or a significant change in mental status.


Read the 6 months carefully. First Coast measures it from the last time the patient was seen or treated, not from the last evaluation, and says routine re-evaluation of chronic patients isn't medically necessary. So a patient in continuous weekly therapy doesn't earn a new 90791 at month seven, while a patient admitted to inpatient psychiatric care at month four can get one, if the note says why.


Payer Limit Exceptions Source


**Medicare** (First Coast, WPS) Once at onset of illness, then after a treatment break of about 6 months. Once per day. Inpatient psychiatric admission, significant change in mental status, separate informant evaluations on different days L33252, L34616, A57480


**Indiana Medicaid** (IHCP) 1 unit of 90791 or 90792 per member, per provider, per rolling 12 months without prior authorization 2 units when a physician or HSPP and another BH practitioner each evaluate the member. More with prior authorization. IHCP Behavioral Health Services module, version 4.6 (October 2026), citing 405 IAC 5-20-8(14)


**Ohio Medicaid** 1 encounter per recipient, per billing provider, per calendar year More with prior authorization. SUD assessments are capped separately at 2 per calendar year per billing agency. Ohio Admin. Code 5160-27-02


Notice the unit of measure. Indiana counts per provider over a rolling year, Ohio per billing provider over a calendar year. Commercial plans set their own frequency edits, often per member per year, so read the current reimbursement policy for each plan. A patient evaluated in December and readmitted in February is fine under Ohio's count and over the limit under Indiana's. Build the frequency edit for each payer, not one house rule.


## Same-day rules: E/M, psychotherapy and NCCI


The 2026 NCCI Policy Manual is explicit. Because psychotherapy includes continuing psychiatric evaluation, 90791 and 90792 aren't separately reportable with individual, group, family, crisis or other psychotherapy codes for the same date. E/M codes such as 99202 to 99215 "shall not be reported with either." A modifier doesn't change that policy.


Billed on the same date by the same provider With 90791 or 90792? Rule


E/M visit (99202 to 99215 and others) No NCCI manual, Chapter XI


Psychotherapy 90832 to 90838, family 90846 and 90847, group 90853 No NCCI manual, Chapter XI


Crisis psychotherapy 90839, 90840 No NCCI manual, A57520, A57480


Interactive complexity +90785 Yes, with a documented qualifying factor L33252, A57480


Alcohol or substance structured assessment and intervention G0396, G0397 No NCCI manual, Chapter XI


Neurobehavioral status exam 96116, 96121 No NCCI manual, Chapter XI


Psychological testing and evaluation 96130 to 96146 Yes, if distinct, with no time counted twice NCCI manual, Chapter XI


NCCI edits apply per provider: same provider, same patient, same date. A therapist's 90791 and a primary care physician's E/M that day don't collide. Indiana Medicaid goes further for two-clinician intakes, allowing a second evaluation unit when a physician or HSPP and another BH practitioner each evaluate the member.


Run a multidisciplinary intake with each clinician on their own line, NPI and note, and book the first psychotherapy session for a later date. Indiana bars psychotherapy on the evaluation day without limiting that to the same clinician.


## When the 90785 add-on is allowed


90785 pays for communication factors that make the service harder, not for a harder patient. First Coast's LCD and the Indiana Medicaid module list the same four factors, and the record must show at least one:


- **Maladaptive communication** among participants, such as high anxiety, high reactivity, repeated questions or disagreement, that complicates care.
- **Caregiver emotions or behaviors** that interfere with carrying out the treatment plan.
- **A sentinel event** with a mandated report to a third party, discussed with the patient and other participants.
- **Play equipment, physical devices, an interpreter or a translator** used to overcome barriers with a patient who isn't fluent in the same language or lacks expressive language skills.


It rides on 90791, 90792, psychotherapy (90832 to 90838) or group psychotherapy (90853). It isn't reported with crisis psychotherapy, and A57480 bars it with an E/M visit when no psychotherapy is reported. It adds $14.70 nationally in 2026. Small per claim. Across a year of child and family intakes, missing it adds up.


The record test is specific. First Coast wants the rationale, the adaptations used and treatment recommendations, and A57520 says 90785 shouldn't be billed when the patient can't communicate by any means. "Parent present" doesn't qualify. "Parents interrupted and contradicted each other about the symptom timeline, so each was interviewed separately for 20 minutes" does.


## What the record must show for each code


First Coast's LCD lists what the evaluation record should contain, a fair proxy for what other reviewers check. For whether the services that follow get paid, see our[medical necessity documentation guide](https://blog.adentris.com/medical-necessity-documentation-behavioral-health/) .


Element 90791 90792 What reviewers look for


Reason for evaluation, referral source Yes Yes Chief complaint in the patient's words, and who referred


History of present illness Yes Yes How long the symptoms have existed, not just a diagnosis


Psychiatric, medical, social and family history Yes Yes Prior treatment and hospitalizations, substance use, family psychiatric history


Current medications Yes Yes, with decisions A reconciled list. For 90792, what was started, changed or stopped, and why


Mental status exam Complete Complete Every domain described, not "WNL" on a checklist


Strengths and liabilities Yes Yes Something the treatment plan can build on


Diagnostic impression Yes Yes ICD-10-CM codes that match the narrative and the claim


Treatment plan or recommendations Yes Yes Methods, anticipated length, measurable goals


Physical exam, prescribing, labs Not part of the code As indicated Exam elements tied to the clinical question, orders, results reviewed


Informants If used If used Who and their relationship. If seen instead of the patient, the specific reason


Interactive complexity If 90785 billed If 90785 billed The qualifying factor and the adaptation used


We'd add two items the LCD doesn't list. Document a suicide and violence risk assessment, because an evaluation without one is hard to defend in any review. And for SUD, record quantity, frequency, route and last use for each substance, so the evaluation supports the level of care decision that follows.

Biopsychosocial assessment template (Word)


An editable template for the intake assessment that feeds the diagnostic evaluation, so history, mental status and recommendations are captured before the evaluation note is written.

## 2026 Medicare payment, place of service and telehealth


These are 2026 national amounts from CMS Physician Fee Schedule data at the $33.4009 conversion factor that applies to most clinicians. Qualifying APM participants get $33.5675. Your MAC applies a geographic adjustment, so treat these as reference points.


Code 2026 office (non-facility) 2026 facility 2025 office 2025 facility


**90791** $173.35 $137.28 $166.91 $142.97


**90792** $202.08 $159.32 $187.93 $163.67


**+90785** $14.70 $11.69 $14.23 $12.29


The split is the 2026 story. Office rates rose and facility rates fell for both evaluation codes, after CMS finalized a policy recognizing greater indirect practice costs in offices than in facilities. In a hospital outpatient department, evaluation payments dropped even as the conversion factor rose. Non-physician practitioners get a share: a CSW's office allowance for 90791 is about $130.01, an NP's for 90792 about $171.77.


To find your rate, search 2026 pricing for the code in the CMS Physician Fee Schedule Look-up Tool and pick your MAC locality. Use the non-facility price for office visits and home telehealth, the facility price for facility settings, then apply the practitioner percentage. Check again each January.


### Telehealth basics


All three codes are on the Medicare Telehealth Services List, and CMS covers behavioral health telehealth to the home permanently. Bill POS 10 when the patient is at home, paid at the non-facility rate, and POS 02 elsewhere. Add modifier 93 for audio-only visits, which Medicare allows for behavioral health at home, and FQ for audio-only services from an RHC or FQHC. Medicaid and commercial plans set their own POS and modifier rules, including modifier 95.


As of November 2026, CMS's Telehealth FAQ (updated October 8, 2026) says the in-person visit requirement for mental health telehealth takes effect after December 31, 2027. Patients who start home telehealth before then will need an in-person visit every 12 months after that date.


## Common denials and how to fix them


Typical CARC What happened Fix


**CO-97** or **CO-236** 90791 or 90792 billed with psychotherapy, an E/M or a crisis code on the same date by the same provider Bill only the evaluation that date, or recode the visit as E/M plus psychotherapy if that's what happened. Don't force the pair through with 59.


**CO-119** The payer's evaluation limit for the period was reached Check the last evaluation date and provider before intake. Request prior authorization, or show a new episode.


**CO-151** The payer sees a repeat evaluation as too frequent Appeal with the note showing the treatment break, the admission or the change in mental status


**CO-8** , **CO-170** or **CO-185** Provider-type mismatch: 90792 by a clinician without medical scope, or an NPI or taxonomy that doesn't fit the code Rebill 90791 if medical services were out of scope, or fix enrollment and taxonomy. Never move the service to another clinician's NPI to get paid.


**CO-107** 90785 without a qualifying primary service, for example with an E/M alone or a crisis code Remove 90785, or bill it on the same claim as the code it supports


**CO-50** Evaluation not supported as medically necessary, often a repeat with no stated reason Show the psychiatric illness or symptoms, and why an evaluation was needed now


**CO-5** or **CO-4** POS or telehealth modifier doesn't fit the payer's rules Correct the POS and the 93, FQ or 95 modifier, then send a corrected claim


Track these by root cause, not by code. If CO-97 or CO-236 keeps landing on intake days, fix the scheduling template. If CO-8 clusters on one clinician, it's an enrollment problem, and no appeal will solve it. Our[CO-50 appeal guide](https://blog.adentris.com/co-50-denial-medical-necessity-behavioral-health/) includes a letter template, and our[CARC guide](https://blog.adentris.com/behavioral-health-denial-codes-carc-guide/) covers the rest of the list.


## Pre-bill checklist for evaluation claims


1. **Right code for the work.** Documented medical services mean 90792. Otherwise, 90791.
2. **Right code for the clinician.** License, payer enrollment and taxonomy support it.
3. **No same-day conflicts.** No psychotherapy, crisis, E/M, G0396, G0397, 96116 or 96121 by the same provider that date.
4. **One unit,** unless a separate informant evaluation happened on a different date.
5. **Frequency checked** against the payer's period: rolling year, calendar year or 365 days.
6. **Any repeat explained:** a treatment break, an admission or a change in mental status.
7. **90785 earned:** a named qualifying factor and the adaptation used.
8. **Telehealth complete:** POS, modifier, modality and patient location documented.
9. **Signed and dated** with credentials before the claim goes out.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between CPT 90791 and 90792?**


90791 is a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. 90792 is the same evaluation with medical services, such as physical exam elements, prescribing medication, or ordering and reviewing labs. Bill 90792 only when that medical work was done and the clinician's license covers it.


**Can a therapist or LCSW bill 90792?**


Generally no. 90792 includes medical services, so physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants and clinical nurse specialists bill it within state scope. LCSWs, counselors, marriage and family therapists and most psychologists bill 90791. Indiana Medicaid is one exception that lets an HSPP render 90792.


**How often can 90791 be billed?**


Medicare contractors allow it once at the onset of illness, with a repeat after a treatment break of about 6 months, an inpatient psychiatric admission or a significant change in mental status, and never more than once a day. Indiana Medicaid allows one per member, per provider, per rolling 12 months without prior authorization, and Ohio Medicaid one per billing provider per calendar year.


**Can you bill 90791 and 90837 on the same day?**


Not for the same provider under Medicare. The 2026 NCCI Policy Manual says 90791 and 90792 are not separately reportable with individual, group, family, crisis or other psychotherapy codes on the same date, and E/M codes cannot be reported with either. Schedule the first psychotherapy session for a later date.


**Is 90791 a timed code?**


No. Neither 90791 nor 90792 has a time in its descriptor, so the evaluation is one unit whether it takes 45 minutes or two hours. Separate evaluations with the patient and with informants on different days can each be reported.


**How much does Medicare pay for 90791 in 2026?**


The 2026 national amount is $173.35 in an office and $137.28 in a facility, before geographic adjustment. For 90792 it is $202.08 and $159.32. Social workers, marriage and family therapists and counselors get 75% of the clinical psychologist amount, and NPs, PAs and CNSs 85% of the physician amount.
